False excision objection: interiors are relative to the ambient pair space, exactly int_X(A) in the cited excision theorem. With original closed disks D_i strictly inside larger disks D_i+, cl(D² minus union D_i+) is contained in the relatively open subset D² minus union D_i of P. Outer-boundary points therefore belong to int_D²(P). Likewise for B=D²×I, enlarging the relative product tubes N_i gives cl(B minus union N_i+) contained in B minus union N_i, relatively open and contained in X_tau. At endpoint caps only the annular shell remains in X_tau, matching (I×D²,I×S¹); the cap interiors are removed by the relative-interior tube definition. Excision, interval contraction, and the pair exact sequence give H2(X_tau)=0 and meridian-basis H1, naturally at both ends. Read the full current proof, tube Definition, exact excision statement, producer contract and manifest. No repair is needed; the historical counterexample also confuses relative and absolute interior.
